matcher requires a catch all to be last. the dollar sign question a filesystem search found no route files whose names require a $ path convention. in the inspected derech code, dollar prefixed names serve a different purpose: $i — request/server context vessel. $ get — parsed query/input data. $ post — parsed submitted body data. $ delete — parsed delete oriented input where used. $u — commonly a user/identity object in some modules. therefore do not translate a route like :alias into $alias . they are different layers. leading and trailing slashes routing/routeforms.js normalizes route aliases with common leading/trailing slash forms. this is why route tables may store keys such as balance while the mounted public route is documented as /api/wallet/balance. derech mounting the searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he routes the awtsmoos sends a path through filesystem and derech, both visible and concealed; awtsmoos.com becomes navigable when url, parameter, and source are all revealed. this section explains how to travel from a browser url to the source that serves it. public filesystem routes the dynamic server's default public root is geelooy. therefore a public url such as /login, /os, /apps/code, or /games/... normally begins by resolving inside the corresponding geelooy/... path. directory index.html files are common entry points, but dynamic derech behavior can intercept or augment a request. use public routes.md for major human facing areas and ../generated/public route inventory.md for the immediate directory inventory. dynamic/api routes derech files named awtsmoos.derech.js are discovered by walking upward from the request's physical path. a derech can return route definitions with exact path strings or colon parameters. api mounts are inventoried in ../generated/derech mounts.md. dynamic parameters :name matches exactly one segment. a terminal :name captures the remainder. catch all parameters must be the final route part. dollar prefixed request variables are not url syntax. read dynamic paths.md for the exact distinction. url lookup workflow 1. if the url starts with /api/, search ../generated/api route atlas.md. 2. otherwise map its first segment to geelooy/ /. 3. look for index.html, client scripts, and nested directories. 4. search ancestors for awtsmoos.derech.js if behavior is dynamic. 5. if the feature uses websockets, also inspect ayzarim/awtsmoosdynamicserver/websocket/. 6. use url to source.md for common examples. do not confuse these three things filesystem url path — source location under public geelooy/. derech route pattern — an exact or colon parameterized dynamic handler. request data vessel — $i, $ get, $ post, $ delete, headers, cookies, body, or auth state.

title: Security and Trust Boundaries
excerpt: B"H Boruch Hashem Blessed is He Security and Trust Boundaries The Awtsmoos renews every request and every identity; Awtsmoos.com therefore separates what the server knows from what a browser, script, socket message, URL or provider merely claims. Canonical session covenant ayzarim/awtsmoosDynamicServer/server/authSetup
searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he security and trust boundaries the awtsmoos renews every request and every identity; awtsmoos.com therefore separates what the server knows from what a browser, script, socket message, url or provider merely claims. canonical session covenant ayzarim/awtsmoosdynamicserver/server/authsetup.js loads one configured secret, constructs the auth verifier, installs http session middleware, and gives the same verifier plus cookie parser to the websocket layer. http and socket transports therefore share authentication machinery while parsing cookies at their own boundaries. if no configured secret exists, auth installation is skipped. if the configured secret module cannot be loaded, the inspected fallback object contains nokey: "no security"; treat configuration of this path as security critical deployment behavior rather than ordinary feature code. trusted identity sources different subsystems accept different authenticated evidence: signed browser session; verified social api key; oauth bearer token; verified tunnel control api key; server attached websocket client identity. a body/query field such as owner, userid, alias or accountid is not automatically identity simply because it has an identity shaped name. authentication versus authorization authentication answers who the server trusts the caller to be. authorization answers whether that identity may perform the requested action on the target resource. alias ownership, heichel editor roles, tunnel scopes/grants, mission room authority and administrative checks live above the authentication layer. security manuals trust boundaries.md — identity and authorization layers. secrets and config.md — secrets, environment names and documentation rules. realtime security.md — socket admission, identity and protocol boundaries. docs/api/authentication.md — api family authentication detail. docs/websockets/mission rooms.md — concrete pre handshake admission flow. evidence rule generated contract/header/environment indexes help locate security relevant source. they are not a security review. before changing an authorization boundary, inspect source, negative tests, current data/grants and runtime traces appropriate to the subsystem.
